transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place for this. I really don't want to come across as a difficult person or anything, but I've just been dealing with a lot of stress, and I was hoping you could help me. 

Well, for months now, I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is... they're quietly messing with our money and our good name. I know that probably sounds a bit strange to say out loud, and I hate to speak ill of family, but it's just these little things happening. Like, little billing errors will suddenly show up at my work, or someone at our church will just start acting really funny toward me out of nowhere. And no matter what records anyone pulls up to try and explain it away, I just... I know it ties back to them. 

I'm sorry to just unload all that right away. Is that... is that the sort of thing we can talk about here? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

When people have shown you records or explanations that don't support your concerns about your husband's family, how do you make sense of that information? Do you think maybe you could be mistaken, or do you feel certain that they're somehow involved despite what the records show?

That's a really fair question. And, um... honestly, I really wish I was mistaken. I've tried so hard to tell myself that I'm just being silly, because I don't want to be the kind of person who points fingers at her own in-laws. I hate conflict. But... well, since I work as a billing clerk myself, I know how easily things can be made to look perfectly fine on paper. 

So when someone shows me a record that supposedly proves nothing is wrong, I just... I know it's not the whole story. Even without the paper proof, I am certain they're behind it. It's just too much of a coincidence, you know? The little errors that keep popping up at my job, and the way people at church are suddenly so cold to me. It all connects back to his family quietly trying to ruin our finances and our reputation. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely stubborn or unreasonable. I'm really trying to be objective about it, and I'd love nothing more than to be wrong. Am I making sense to you so far?

When you think about how your husband's family is doing all of this, do you have a clear understanding of exactly how they're accomplishing it—like, what specific methods or steps they're using to cause these billing errors and influence people at church?

Oh... um, that's a very good question, Doctor. Honestly, I... I don't exactly know the step-by-step of how they're pulling it all off. I know that probably makes me sound a little silly, and I'm really sorry I don't have a better answer for you. 

I try not to pry too much or go digging around, because I really don't want to cause a scene or be a nuisance to anyone. I just know they have their ways. Maybe they're just quietly saying things to people at church when I'm not around, or... or maybe they know someone who works with the software for our billing system? I'm just not entirely sure of the exact methods they use to make it happen. 

I really hope it's okay that I don't have all the specifics figured out. I know I should probably have all the facts completely straight before bringing something like this up to a doctor. Am I... am I still giving you the kind of information you need? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
Besides your husband's family and the issues at work and church, do you have concerns that other people or groups are also working against you or trying to harm you in some way?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... no, definitely not. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I think the whole world is out to get me. I know how terrible that would sound, and I promise I'm not... I'm not like that at all. 

It's really just this one specific situation with my in-laws. Everyone else in my life, like my neighbors and the other people I interact with, they're all perfectly lovely. I don't have any worries about anyone else trying to harm me or anything like that. 

Is... is that okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right and not making things sound worse than they are, or making you think I'm just pointing fingers at everyone. Does that help clarify things?
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you couldn't hear or see, or have you had any unusual sensory experiences related to what your in-laws are doing?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. Um... I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. I know sometimes people who are... well, going through a lot of stress might experience things like that, but I haven't. 

I just... I just notice the things that are actually happening, like the billing errors and the way people act. But I don't see or hear anything unusual. I really hope that's a good thing, right? I mean, I'm trying so hard to keep my feet on the ground through all of this. I just want to be as helpful and accurate for you as possible. Am I... am I still doing okay with these questions?

If your husband or someone you trust very much sat down with you and said they had thoroughly investigated and found absolutely no evidence that your in-laws were involved in any of these problems, would you be able to consider that maybe you've been mistaken about this, or would you still feel completely certain they're behind it?

Oh... um... that's a really tough question. I... I know the right answer, the one I probably *should* give you, is that I would just say 'oh, okay' and let it go. I really don't want to come across as stubborn or, you know, unreasonable. I know how bad that looks, and I hate being difficult. 

But... honestly? I’m here because for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. Even if my husband looked and said he couldn't find anything... like when those little billing errors show up at my work, or someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me... I just... no matter what records anyone pulls up or what they say they couldn't find, I know it ties back to them. 

I feel terrible saying that, I really do. I know it makes me sound awful and unyielding to not just take his word for it. I'm sorry, is... is it okay that I'm being this honest with you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the truth, even if it's not the best-sounding answer. Am I still doing okay?

When you think about your in-laws being involved in all of this, on a scale where 0 means 'I could be completely wrong' and 100 means 'I am absolutely certain beyond any doubt,' where would you say you fall?

Oh, gosh... a number. Um... I really, really want to say something like fifty, or maybe seventy-five? Just because... well, saying one hundred makes me sound so... so closed-minded, doesn't it? And I promise I'm usually a very open and reasonable person. I hate sounding like I'm just rigidly stuck in my ways. 

But... um... if I'm being completely truthful with you—and I know I need to be—it's... it's a hundred. Because, like I was just saying, I’ve been trying for months to get people to understand that his family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. Every time those little billing errors show up at work, or someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me... it just confirms it. No matter what records anyone pulls up to try and prove otherwise, I just know in my heart it ties back to them. 

I'm so sorry, I know a hundred probably isn't what a doctor wants to hear. It makes me sound terrible, doesn't it? Is... is it going to be held against me that I'm that certain? I really am trying to be a good patient and give you the right answers, I promise.

When you say you're a hundred percent certain, do you mean that there is literally no possible way you could be wrong, or do you mean you're very confident but you can imagine a scenario—even if it seems unlikely—where you might have misunderstood what's happening?

Oh... um... that's... that's such a hard question to answer without sounding... well, without sounding crazy or difficult. I really don't want to be difficult. I know the right thing to say is that there's always a chance I could be wrong. That's what a normal, reasonable person would say, right? And I really try to be reasonable.

But... if I'm being completely honest—and I know you need me to be honest—I just... I can't see any way I could be wrong. I mean, I've spent months trying to explain this to people. When those billing errors happen at work, or when the people at church start acting strange around me... it's not just a coincidence. It's his family. They're quietly ruining our finances and our reputation. 

I know people can pull up records or show me things that supposedly prove they aren't involved, but... I just know they are. There isn't really a scenario where I just misunderstood it all. It's too connected. 

I'm sorry, I know that's not the answer you probably want. Does that make me sound completely unreasonable? I'm really trying to be helpful, I just... I can't lie and say I might be wrong when I know I'm not. Is that okay?
